deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Riemann does a saddle-point analysis of the phase f = -y s + 1/2 log((1+s)/(1-s)). On the next page he does the same with a different phase. On this page he takes a degenerating Riemann P-function and derives series and asymptotic expansions for the limit equation. The limit equation is equivalent to Weber's parabolic-cylinder (Hermite) equation and to Kummer's confluent equation.

(1) P-scheme, top four lines. Read the third row (0, 1, -1) as the singular points in z = x/n. The first two rows are then the exponent pairs:
- at z=0: 0 and 1/2;
- at z=1: n/2 and -n/2+1/4;
- at z=-1: -n/2-alpha/2+1/4 and n/2+alpha/2.
The exponents sum to 1, as Riemann's condition requires (my check). The meaning of the fourth row (1, 2, 0) is unclear. It may give the products (a-b)(a-c) etc., but this is uncertain.

(2) Behaviour as n -> oo. He writes the factors (1-x/n)^{n/2} and (1+x/n)^{n/2+alpha/2}, a factor (n/x)^n, and their limits e^{-x/2} and e^{+x/2}. He also writes e^{-x} and e^{+x}, which are the true large-x behaviours of the limit equation. My verification: put Riemann's differential equation for this P-function in the variable x and let n -> oo with x fixed. The equation tends to
  x u'' + 1/2 u' + (alpha - x) u = 0.   (*)
The page itself never writes (*). It is forced by the next step: substituting u = e^{-eps x} v into (*) gives exactly the v-equation on the page.
(*) is Weber/Hermite in disguise: with x = t^2 it becomes u_tt + 4(alpha - t^2) u = 0.

(3) Substitution u = e^{-eps x} v, with the factor e^{-eps x} suppressed in the derivatives:
- u' ~ v' - eps v;
- u'' ~ v'' - 2 eps v' + eps^2 v.
This gives x v'' + (1/2 - 2 eps x) v' + ((eps^2 - 1) x + alpha - eps/2) v = 0.
Choosing eps^2 = 1 kills the x-term. What remains is Kummer's equation in z = 2 eps x:
  z w'' + (1/2 - z) w' - (1/4 - alpha/(2 eps)) w = 0.

(4) Euler operator. He notes x d/dlog x and the identity x v'' = (1/x)(v_{theta theta} - v_theta), with theta = log x. This is correct.

(5) Power series v = sum a_mu x^mu. Collecting terms gives
  mu(mu - 1/2) a_mu x^{mu-1} + (-2 eps mu + alpha - eps/2) a_mu x^mu.
The recurrence follows (one wrong index shift is struck out on the page):
  mu(mu - 1/2) a_mu = ((2mu - 3/2) eps -/+ alpha) a_{mu-1}.
Solve it with Pi(s) = Gamma(s+1), multiplying through by Pi(mu) Pi(mu - 1/2):
  a_mu = (2 eps)^mu Pi(mu - 3/4 + alpha/(2 eps)) / (Pi(mu) Pi(mu - 1/2)), up to a constant.
So u = e^{-eps x} times a 1F1(.; 1/2; 2 eps x) series. This is the first displayed term e^{-x eps}(2x eps)^mu Pi(mu - 3/4 + ...)/(Pi mu Pi(mu - 1/2)). He compares it with the finite-n factor (1 + x/n)...

(6) Asymptotic (divergent) series. The third displayed term is
  e^{-x eps} (2x eps)^{-n - 1/4 - alpha/(2 eps)} Pi(n - 1/4 + alpha/(2 eps)) Pi(n - 3/4 + alpha/(2 eps)) / Pi(n).
With a = 1/4 + alpha/(2 eps) and b = 1/2, this is z^{-a-n} Gamma(a+n) Gamma(a-b+1+n)/n!. That is the general term of the standard large-z expansion of the Tricomi solution U(a, 1/2, z) of Kummer's equation, i.e. the parabolic-cylinder asymptotic series.
The second displayed term, e^{-x eps}(2x eps)^{(-)mu} Pi(mu-1) Pi(mu - 1/2 ...)/Pi(mu + 1/4 - ...), appears to be an intermediate attempt at the same reversed (descending) series.
Together with the surrounding pages, the aim seems to be: obtain the asymptotics of these functions (of the hypergeometric P-function for a large parameter n) by the saddle-point method, and compare them with the explicit series.

(7) Upside-down marginal notes (m z = -d rho/d log rho, m + M = n, ...) are unrelated and largely illegible.
errors: Sign of alpha. From the page's own coefficient (-2 eps mu + alpha - eps/2), the recurrence must read mu(mu-1/2) a_mu = ((2mu-3/2) eps - alpha) a_{mu-1}. That gives Pi(mu - 3/4 - alpha/(2 eps)), i.e. Kummer parameter a = 1/4 - alpha/(2 eps). The page writes +alpha / +alpha/(2 eps), carried consistently into the asymptotic term. Either this is a sign slip or the sign of alpha is defined differently in (*); the image is ambiguous at the '=' in the recurrence line.
In u = e^{-eps x} v, the derivatives u' = v' - eps v and u'' = v'' - 2 eps v' + eps^2 v omit the common factor e^{-eps x}. This is harmless shorthand.
The asymptotic term omits the alternating sign (-1)^n of the standard expansion z^{-a} sum (a)_n (a-b+1)_n/n! (-z)^{-n}, unless it is absorbed in the choice of eps.
The first trial index shift for the recurrence ('(mu+1)(mu+1/2) a_{mu+1}') was struck out by Riemann himself and corrected.

results.what: Confluence of a Riemann P-function with singular points 0, n, -n and exponents (0, 1/2), (n/2, -n/2+1/4), (-n/2-alpha/2+1/4, n/2+alpha/2) to x u'' + u'/2 + (alpha - x) u = 0 as n -> oo, with (1 -/+ x/n)^{n/2} -> e^{-/+ x/2}.
results.modern_name: confluence of the hypergeometric (Riemann) equation to the confluent / Weber (parabolic cylinder) equation
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer (1836) for 1F1; Weber (1869) and Hermite (1864) for the parabolic cylinder/Hermite equation; systematic confluence of P-functions later (Klein, Whittaker 1903)

results.what: Substitution u = e^{-eps x} v with eps^2 = 1, reducing to Kummer's equation; power-series solution with Gamma-ratio coefficients (a 1F1(1/4 -/+ alpha/(2 eps); 1/2; 2 eps x) series).
results.modern_name: Kummer function M(a, 1/2, 2x); Kummer transformation relating eps = +1 and -1

results.what: Descending (divergent) series e^{-eps x} sum (2 eps x)^{-a-n} Gamma(a+n) Gamma(a+1/2+n)/n!.
results.modern_name: asymptotic expansion of Tricomi U(a, 1/2, z) / parabolic cylinder functions
results.usually_credited_to: Stokes / Weber / Hermite (1850s-60s); Poincaré's formal theory of asymptotic series (1886)

results.what: Euler-operator identity x v'' = (1/x)(v_{theta theta} - v_theta), theta = log x.

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's work on hypergeometric functions (1857), P-functions and the saddle-point method (1863 fragment) is well known, so treating confluent and parabolic-cylinder limits is not out of character. Two details are a notable unpublished glimpse if the bundle date (1853) is right: an explicit P-function confluence to the Weber/Hermite-type equation, and the pairing of its convergent series with the descending asymptotic series. These would predate Weber 1869 and Hermite 1864. Still, the computations are routine and Kummer and Stokes had related material.

transcription_corrections: Row '0 1 -1' is most plausibly the list of singular points (0, 1, -1 in the variable x/n) of the P-scheme, with the first two rows as the exponent pairs (0, 1/2), (n/2, -n/2+1/4), (-n/2-alpha/2+1/4, n/2+alpha/2).
The first line has a separate factor (1 - x/n)^{n/2} at the far left; the main group reads (1-x/n)^{n/2}(1+x/n)^{n/2+alpha/2}(n/x)^n.

In the asymptotic term, both Pi(n-1/4+...) and Pi(n-3/4+...) appear to stand in the numerator with Pi(n) in the denominator. It is not Pi(n-1/4)/(Pi(n-3/4) Pi n). The second Pi factor is written on the same line as the d^2v/dx^2 term of the ODE.
Parameter terms written 'alpha/(2 eps)' may be written eps*alpha/2 on the page; these are equal since eps^2 = 1.
The second displayed term may have exponent (2x eps)^{-mu} rather than ^{mu}. Its last numerator factor reads like Pi(mu - 1/2 ...), not 'Pi(mu - 1/2 x)'.
The final line is probably 'eps 2 (mu - 3/4 + alpha/(2 eps)) a_{mu-1}', i.e. the right-hand side of the recurrence factored as 2 eps(mu - 3/4 + ...). It is not eps 2^mu Pi(...).
The ODE term 'x' before d^2v/dx^2 is present on the page.
